title: a `with` statement is FORBIDDEN in authored `.sm` — the third classification bucket, not merely a form that contributes the `TypeScript` requirement
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Dynamic Features': 'Every relevant TypeScript or JavaScript runtime feature MUST be assigned one classification: 1. portable across TypeScript and native targets; 2. valid but contributing the `TypeScript` requirement; 3. forbidden in authored `.sm` source.' docs/DECISIONS.md 'TypeScript and native classification' (Locked) lists the same three. The other cases in this area pin buckets 1 and 2 — universal globals and ordinary code are portable, `any` and `eval` are valid-but-contributing — and this is the area's only case for bucket 3 that comes from the portability classifier itself rather than from a frontend ownership rule. The distinction matters: a form in bucket 2 must COMPILE (18/any-is-usable-and-not-forbidden pins that `any` is 'not globally forbidden'), so a compiler that filed `with` in bucket 2 would accept it, and one that filed `any` in bucket 3 would reject a documented escape hatch. `with` is the clearest member of bucket 3: it makes every identifier in its body dynamically scoped, which no static requirement row or native lowering can model.
